Central Bank Reinforcement Act
Central Bank Reinforcement Act

The Central Bank Reinforcement Act led by Edith Agnoc and the GNA intends to bolster the strength and stability of Sordland's national currency and bolster the overall economy. The Grand National Assembly advocates for the following measures: Section I mandates the accumulation of foreign exchange reserves. By buying foreign currencies, especially those of Sordland's main trading partners, the Central Bank can exert more control over the value of our currency. Section II outlines the adoption of a prudent fiscal policy. By reducing the national debt and limiting budget deficits, the country can present itself as a more stable economic entity, attracting foreign investment and improving our credit rating, which in turn would enable us to borrow at lower interest rates, if necessary. Section III proposes increased legal and informational support for industries with high export potential, such as our emerging electronics sector in Gelsord, wine production in Borin, and pharmaceutical manufacturing in Lachaven. By increasing exports, the demand for our currency on the international market will rise, thus strengthening its value. [-1 Government Budget]
The CBR bill has been passed by the GNA.
Energy Inflation Reduction Act
Energy Inflation Reduction Act

The Energy Inflation Reduction Act aims to address the recent surge in energy prices due to foreign entities' manipulation of key energy companies. The Grand National Assembly proposes these countermeasures: Section I establishes a temporary price cap on gas prices to prevent extreme hikes in energy costs for Sordish citizens. This measure ensures immediate relief for consumers without causing too drastic a shock to the energy market. Section II calls for the negotiation of bilateral agreements with energy-rich countries for stable and reasonably priced energy supplies. This strategy would insulate Sordland from price manipulation tactics and ensure a more stable energy market. Section III outlines the strategic expansion and modernization of domestic energy production capabilities. By investing in our own coal and natural gas facilities, we can reduce our dependence on foreign energy supplies and insulate our economy from external price shocks. This effort would also create jobs and stimulate domestic economic growth. [-1 Government Budget]
